title: Do Not Enter
subtitle: The woods have eyes, and they see everything.

items.text: Nearby Forest, Temporary Stop

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Apologies for the wait.
Lower your weapons. It's Iglika!
Shadows part, young men emerge. Recognizing the conductress, they lower their rifles.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: I prefer Corvus. It's more familiar to me.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Are they all our people?
She checks their faces, easing only when she sees no strangers among them.

items.speaker: Watch Soldier
items.text: Yes, no others, just as planned.

items.speaker: Watch Soldier
items.text: Pyrrhos's men are patrolling ahead.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Good. Finish this quickly.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: The passengers believe we're clearing snow ahead of the train.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Is Pyrrhos holding up his end?

items.speaker: Watch Soldier
items.text: Yes. He'll let you through when the train arrives.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Good. And the "cargo"?

items.speaker: Watch Soldier
items.text: In the carriage over there, in the woods.

items.speaker: Watch Soldier
items.text: We've got horses to pull it over.

items.speaker: Watch Soldier
items.text: This way. It'll keep you out of sight.
At her word, the men hurry down the forked path by the tracks.

items.speaker: Watch Soldier
items.text: Come on, follow us!
She steps forward, but her coat hem is tugged.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Conductress, I ...

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Got it.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Don't worry. I'll be back.
The conductress drapes a newly-made scarf over the girl's shoulders until it has all but buried her face.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: So soft. Thank you, Conductress.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: I don't want you to catch a chill.

items.speaker: Watch Soldier
items.text: Iglika—
Patting her shoulder, she walks alone into the shadows.

items.speaker: Watch Soldier
items.text: One, two, three!

items.speaker: Watch Soldier
items.text: Phew! Done. That was a heavy one.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Alright, time for an inventory check.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: She's added another carriage?
Semmelweis blends into the dark shadows of the trees, examining the train.
A new carriage is pulled up and secretly attached behind the rear cabin.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: What's it carrying? Guns? Ammunition? Controlled substances?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: And those don't look like Serbian troops.
She waits until the soldiers disperse, leaving only two behind.
Aima lowers her head and clutches her scarf.
Then, she suddenly collapses to her knees.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Aima?
The snow falls constantly and heavily.
Their figures lean together in the storm, like ghosts rooted among the trees.
In that moment, all else melts away. The world is only the two of them.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: I'm sorry, I ...

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Shh-shh. I know. I know.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Silly girl. Shouldn't have gotten so close.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: What are they ... Could it be ...
The investigator, hidden in shadow, frowns as she keens her eyes.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Need to get confirmation.
Freeze.
Hands up where I can see them.
She raises her hands.
Turn around.
Two soldiers stagger before her, faces ghostly and haggard, like two white flames drifting in the night.

items.speaker: Patrol Soldier II
items.text: Good. Don't do anything stupid.

items.speaker: Patrol Soldier II
items.text: What did you see just now?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I saw ...
She flicks her toe, kicking a stone into one soldier's knee.

items.speaker: Patrol Soldier I
items.text: Ugh!
He cries out, buckling to the ground.
She lunges, seizing his weapon in the same instant, turning it on the other.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: My turn now.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Hands up where I can see them.
Two young soldiers lie unconscious in the snow.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Something's wrong with these soldiers. Slow movements, unsteady steps, and their faces ... oddly pale ...

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Hmm, no bullets in either gun. That can't just be a mistake.
She checks their gear: empty rifles, unmarked tags, and a trinket that draws her eye.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Same shape and size. This looks to be the item the conductress gave that soldier at the station earlier.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Manus Vindictae. Finally, you rear your head.
She runs her fingers over the familiar symbol, then pulls her communicator from her coat and presses the button.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Investigator Semmelweis to Foundation, mission number 0073-MV.

items.speaker: Foundation Operator
items.text: Go ahead, Investigator.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Progress update: I've found a Manus Vindictae insignia on a soldier at a station near Belgrade.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: The conductress of the "Danube Dawn" has undertaken suspicious dealings with these soldiers, stopping the train on the pretext of "the railway being blocked by the snow" in order to secretly add an additional carriage.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I now have reason to believe that the conductress is collaborating with Manus Vindictae. Whatever's in that carriage may be related to our blood-sucking target.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: One more thing: I've lost contact with all members of Squad 77.

items.speaker: Foundation Operator
items.text: Mission 0073-MV report received. We will continue our search for Squad 77. Please proceed with your mission, Investigator.
Report finished, she snaps the device shut.
She looks up at the dark sky. The storm is easing.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Been out here a while. Any longer and I might start to raise suspicion.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Time to head back.
Time passes slowly.
A few passengers stir awake with the stop; some step out of their cabins, whispering in the darkness.

items.speaker: Train Steward
items.text: All passengers, please remain in your rooms. The train is about to depart, and we will reach the border checkpoint soon!
The steward moves between cars, calming their unease.
Between two cars, he sees one door ajar, wind blowing snow inside.

items.speaker: Train Steward
items.text: Hm? Why is the door open?

items.speaker: Train Steward
items.text: Wait a minute, there's something underneath.

items.speaker: Unwell Passenger
items.text: *coughing*
A passenger leans there, coughing hard, drawing the attention of the steward.

items.speaker: Unwell Passenger
items.text: *cough* Excuse me, when is the train leaving?

items.speaker: Train Steward
items.text: Oh! Apologies, sir. In about five, no, ten minutes.

items.speaker: Unwell Passenger
items.text: Okay.
He lowers his head with dejection.
When the steward leaves, his eyes roll, lips twitching with a guttural rasp.
*groan*
Low rumbles drown voices, shouts, any stray sound in the train.
The "Danube Dawn" rolls on into the storm, laden with passengers.
